reading_comprehension_tests.excerpt: One morning, when Gregor Samsa woke from troubled dreams, he found himself transformed in his bed into a horrible vermin. questions.question_text: What metaphor does Ishmael use to describe his profound psychological depression?

options.A: A dark tempest on the ocean
options.B: A damp, drizzly November in his soul
options.D: An iron cage around his heart

questions.explanation: He explicitly calls his inner mood 'a damp, drizzly November in my soul.'

questions.question_text: What morbid physical habit does Ishmael engage in when his dark mood takes over?

options.B: Pausing before coffin warehouses and joining the back of funerals
options.D: Staring at dead leaves falling from trees

questions.explanation: He notes 'involuntarily pausing before coffin warehouses, and bringing up the rear of every funeral I meet.'

questions.question_text: What absurd impulse must Ishmael exercise 'strong moral principle' to restrain?

options.B: Methodically knocking people's hats off in the street
options.C: Screaming loudly in quiet public places
options.D: Jumping off the docks into icy water

questions.explanation: He states it requires moral restraint 'to prevent me from deliberately stepping into the street, and methodically knocking peopleâ€™s hats off.'

questions.question_text: What idiom/phrase does Ishmael use to refer to his bouts of depression or low spirits?
questions.explanation: He refers to when 'my hypos get such an upper hand of me' ('hypos' being short for hypochondria/melancholy).

questions.question_text: What physical benefits does Ishmael humorously attribute to going to sea?

options.B: Driving off the spleen and regulating the circulation
options.C: Improving eyesight and sharpening the mind
options.D: Clearing the lungs and soothing joints

questions.explanation: The text states: 'It is a way I have of driving off the spleen and regulating the circulation.'

questions.question_text: How does the narrator describe his financial situation prior to his journey?

options.A: He was wealthy but greedy for more
options.B: He had little or no money in his purse
options.C: He was deeply in debt to merchants
options.D: He lived comfortably on an inheritance

questions.explanation: The opening lines state he had 'little or no money in my purse.'

questions.question_text: How would you characterize the tone of Ishmael's opening narrative voice?
questions.explanation: Ishmael balances deep existential melancholy with deadpan self-awareness and absurd humor (e.g., knocking off hats), producing a wry, introspective, eccentric tone.
